transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess I came in because I haven’t really been acting like myself since I moved into this messed-up room I’m renting. It’s like every little thing in there is broken or half-broken — leaks, the heat not working right, stuff like that — and I end up staying up trying to fix it or deal with it because if I don’t, nobody else is going to.

Then I’m getting barely any rest, and I go to work the next day already worn out. I do construction, so I can’t really be showing up late or messing up simple stuff, but that’s been happening. Things I normally handle fine, I’m making mistakes on, or I’m dragging myself in late because I was up all night dealing with the room.

And I’ve been snapping at people too. Like coworkers, people around me… I don’t mean to, but I get irritated fast now. It’s just been building up, and I figured maybe I should talk to somebody before it gets worse or I lose my job or something.
Have you noticed these feelings of irritability and low energy occurring even before the move or started only after you moved into this room?

No, I mean… before I moved in there, I was doing pretty normal. I wasn’t walking around irritated all the time or feeling drained like this. Work was work, you know, I’d get tired after a long day, but it made sense. It wasn’t like this constant worn-out feeling.

It really started after I got into that room. At first I thought maybe I just needed to settle in, like moving is always kind of stressful, but then within the first couple weeks I started finding the water damage and realizing the heat wasn’t working right, and that’s when it all started getting to me. Like once those problems showed up and I saw they weren’t getting fixed, that’s when I noticed my mood and energy changing.
Have you found yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even when you’re not thinking about the problems in your room?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say it’s like that exactly. I mean, I’m definitely not in a great mood most of the time lately, but it feels tied to all that stuff with the room. Like if I’m at work or just away from it for a while, I can be okay for bits of time, but then I remember I’ve got to go back there and deal with whatever’s wrong, and it comes right back.

As far as losing interest in things, I haven’t really thought of it that way. I still want to do normal stuff, I think. It’s more like I’m too tired or too frustrated to enjoy it much, if that makes sense. But I don’t think I’m just sitting around feeling down for no reason when I’m not thinking about the room. It’s hard to separate it, though, because that place is kind of always in the back of my head.
Have you had days where you feel down or hopeless even when you’re not thinking about the problems with your room?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly, honestly. I mean, I’ve had bad days, yeah, where I feel pretty low or like, “man, this is never going to get better,” but usually if I really think about it, it’s connected to the room somehow. Like it might not be right in that second that I’m staring at a leak or dealing with the heat or whatever, but it’s still kind of hanging over me.

So I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless out of nowhere. It’s more like I’ll be sitting there trying to have a normal minute, and then it hits me that I’ve got to go back to that place, or I start thinking about how I don’t know when it’s going to be fixed, and then I get that heavy feeling. But if I’m not thinking about it at all — like truly not thinking about it — I don’t think I’m just randomly feeling hopeless for no reason. It’s hard to separate, because it’s kind of always there in the background.

Have you experienced any days where you felt down or lost interest in things even when you weren’t thinking about your housing situation at all—like when you’re at work or distracted with something else?

Yeah… I mean, when I’m at work I can get distracted for a little while, especially if I’m busy carrying stuff or doing something that takes my attention. But it’s not like the feeling is totally separate from the housing thing. The main reason I came in is because ever since I moved into that busted-up room, I’ve been acting different.

Like I’ll be at work and I’m not necessarily standing there thinking, “Oh, the room, the room,” every second, but I’m already worn out because I was up late dealing with some leak or trying to mess with the heat or checking if something got worse. Then I show up dragging, sometimes late, and I’m messing up things I normally handle fine. And when that happens I get even more irritated, because I know I’m not usually like that.

So if you’re asking if I’m just losing interest in stuff out of nowhere, with no connection to the room at all, I don’t think so. It’s more like that situation has me stretched thin, and then even when I’m trying to focus on something else, I’m tired and snapping at people. It follows me around even when I’m not actively thinking about it.
Have you lost interest in or felt less pleasure from activities you used to enjoy, even when you’re not focused on the problems with your room?

I’m honestly not sure I can say it’s happening separate from the room stuff. Like, I still want to enjoy things. If someone asked me, “Do you want to go do something normal, get food, watch something, hang out?” I don’t feel like I don’t care about any of that anymore. It’s more like by the time I get to it, I’m already tense or worn down, and then I don’t get as much out of it.

So I guess, yeah, sometimes things don’t feel as fun lately, but I keep coming back to the same thing — it feels connected. If I’m distracted enough, I can still laugh at something or get into something for a bit. But then my mind drifts back, or I remember I have to go back there, and it kind of kills the mood.

I don’t think I’ve noticed this thing where I’m just not able to enjoy anything even when I’m completely not focused on the room. It’s hard for me to separate it that cleanly, because even when I’m not actively thinking about it, it’s still kind of sitting there in the background.

Have you felt down or lost your motivation even during times when you weren't dealing with the housing problems or thinking about them at all—like when you're at work, hanging out with friends, or doing something you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I mean… I get what you’re asking. I don’t think it’s like I’m just randomly down or unmotivated for no reason when everything else is fine. The reason I came in is because ever since I moved into that busted-up room, I’ve been different.

Like, I’ll stay up late trying to deal with some stupid leak, or messing with the heat, or checking if something got worse, and then the next day I’m dragging myself into work. Sometimes I’m late, sometimes I’m just not sharp, and I mess up stuff I normally wouldn’t mess up. And then I get frustrated because I know I can do the work — I’m not usually like that.

And yeah, even if I’m at work or around people and I’m not actively thinking about the room that exact second, it’s still like I’m carrying the effects of it. I’m tired, I’m irritated, I snap at people more than I should. So it can look like I’ve lost motivation, but to me it feels like that whole room situation has worn me down, and it follows me into everything else.
Have you been feeling like you’re failing at things, or felt excessive guilt or worthlessness about your situation, even when it’s not entirely your fault?

I don’t know if I’d call it worthlessness. Like, I’m not sitting there thinking I’m a terrible person or that everything is my fault. But I do get mad at myself, if that makes sense.

Like when I’m late to work or I mess something up, I’ll think, “Come on, man, get it together.” And then I start feeling like I’m failing at stuff I should be able to handle. But at the same time, part of me knows the whole situation is wearing me down, so it’s not like I fully believe it’s all because I’m useless or something.

I guess there’s some guilt, mostly around not handling it better. Like I keep thinking I should be able to just push through it, because that’s what I usually do. But I wouldn’t say it’s this heavy feeling of being worthless. It’s more frustration with myself, and feeling embarrassed that it’s affecting me this much.
Have there been days when you felt down or had little interest in doing things for most of the day, more days than not, even when you weren't directly thinking about your housing situation?

I mean… most of the day, more days than not, if you’re asking like it’s just there on its own, I don’t know that I’d say it that way. It’s hard for me to separate it from the room, because that’s really when all this started.

Like I came in because ever since I moved into that busted-up place, I’m not acting like myself. I’m staying up trying to deal with stupid stuff that shouldn’t even be my problem — leaks, the heat not working right, checking things over and over because I don’t trust it. Then I’m going into work exhausted, dragging myself in, sometimes late, and I’m messing up things I normally handle fine.

And then because I’m tired and irritated, I snap at people. Not even always about the room right that second, but it’s like I’m already wound up from it. So yeah, there are days where I don’t feel like doing much and I’m kind of down or fed up for a lot of the day, but to me it still feels like it’s coming from that situation wearing me down, not like I just lost interest in life out of nowhere.
Have you had trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much that isn't directly related to the stress of your room situation?

I don’t really know that I can say it’s separate from the room stuff. Like, the sleep problem I notice is mostly because of that situation — I’ll be up listening for noises, checking something, thinking about whether something’s going to leak again, or just feeling keyed up because I don’t feel settled there.

If you mean, like, on a normal night where none of that is on my mind, do I still just randomly have trouble sleeping? I haven’t really noticed that. I’m not sleeping too much either, not like I’m in bed all day or anything. It’s more that my sleep gets messed up when the room stress gets in my head, and then the next day I’m worn out. So… no, I don’t think it’s happening apart from that, at least not that I can tell.
